# llms.txt

Project: Leonaderi Interactive Portfolio World
Repository type: Static Vite + TypeScript + Kaboom single-page app
Primary goal: Preserve the current playable portfolio experience while making small, low-risk improvements.
Secondary goal: Let other developers reuse this repo as a base for their own interactive portfolio worlds.

## Architecture

- `src/main.ts`: game runtime, interaction handling, onboarding, HUD, dialogs, camera, movement, language toggle.
- `src/game/world/mapData.ts`: world layout, tile/collision constants, map objects, NPC coordinates.
- `src/content/glossary.ts`: portfolio POIs, dialogs, links, labels, and world metadata.
- `src/style.css`: all runtime styling for HUD, dialogs, onboarding, and mobile controls.
- `public/assets/`: sprites, map imagery, portraits, and social preview assets.
- `index.html`: app shell and metadata.

## Working Rules

- Treat this as a release-oriented repo: make incremental, reversible edits.
- Do not redesign core gameplay, controls, or map layout unless explicitly asked.
- Prefer data-driven fixes over string-based UI heuristics.
- Keep the app statically hostable; do not introduce required backend services.
- Verify changes with `npm run verify`.

## Deployment

- Build command: `npm run build`
- Output directory: `dist`
- Vercel config exists in `vercel.json`
- GitHub Pages subpath support exists in `vite.config.ts`

## Safe Edit Zones

- Copy and link updates: `src/content/glossary.ts`
- Small UI/runtime fixes: `src/main.ts`, `src/style.css`, `index.html`
- Asset swaps/additions: `public/assets/**`
- Repo documentation: `README.md`, `llms.txt`

## How To Fork This Into A Similar Project

- Replace profile and social preview images first.
- Update `portfolioGlossary` to reflect the new owner, links, and POIs.
- Keep Kaboom runtime changes narrow unless the requested feature truly needs engine work.
- Reuse the existing map/object/NPC structure instead of introducing a second content system.
- Preserve public static hosting compatibility.

## Known Intent

- Keep the project easy to clone, inspect, and redeploy.
- Keep behavior matching the published experience.
- Clean up inconsistencies before broadening scope.
